full_text_zh:
[P1] ＄如果动物有钱了
金钱不是万能的
[美]夏洛特·丹 著 [美]亚当·荣 绘 王思尧 译
中信出版集团

[P2] 金钱是获取快乐的关键！每当我们买到了
自己想要的东西时，都会很开心，对吧？

但大多数动物都发现，猫鼬虽然
是他当中最快乐的一个，可他并没有
花很多钱！这太不可思议了。

[P3] 比如，猫鼬最喜欢的玩具并不是他在圣诞节收到的超级英雄模型，而是这些模型的包装盒。
超级英雄模型确实很酷，但是那些包装盒能满足他的幻想。从太空到深海，他想象着驾驶这艘飞船去任何地方！
幸福指数：10/10 $

[P4] 上个假期，猫鼬和两个好兄弟在海滩露营。实在是太快乐了！
他们所有的食物都是自己采摘和捕获的。露营地甚至连厕所都没有。但猫鼬真正在乎的是能和朋友们在一起。
幸福指数：10/10 $

[P5] 猫鼬知道钱很重要，但他发现自己的快乐并不是来自花钱。
他的快乐来自和谁在一起，来自笑容和回忆，也来自他的感受。金钱买不到这些！所以他想让自己感觉更快乐时，并不需要依赖金钱。

[P6] 但猫鼬以前并不懂得这些道理，他曾经认为金钱才是快乐的源泉。
那时，他觉得钱花得越多，就越快乐。奇怪的是，这种做法反而让他非常不快乐。

[P7] 比如，几年前，猫鼬参加了一个豪华旅行团。那次旅行的费用实在太高了，他的朋友们都负担不起，所以没能参加。
他花钱买各种东西，可还是太无聊了，整个旅程中他都在和朋友们打电话，还很想家。
幸福指数：
2.5/10

[P8] 还有一次，他花了很多钱买了一双漂亮的红鞋，鞋子闪闪发亮，还有气垫呢！他迫不及待地去向朋友们炫耀。
但那双鞋实在是不舒服，后来他再也不穿了。
幸福指数：2/10

[P9] 又有一次，猫鼬去了小镇上最高档的饭店。为了赴宴，他只好穿上燕尾服，还要在用餐时使用各种叉子。
但是吃完后，猫鼬还是很饿，他只好又去买了两个汉堡包。

[P10] 在汉堡店，狐狸看到了穿着燕尾服的猫鼬，问他晚上过得怎么样。

猫鼬忍不住抱怨道：“老兄，我花了这么多钱想让自己快乐，但一点儿用都没有！我不知道该怎么办了，难道我做错了什么吗？”

[P11] 狐狸立刻明白了问题出在哪里。他说："我知道了，我觉得你没有明白快乐从何而来。"

"你可能也没明白，金钱到底是用来做什么的。"

[P12] “钱会让我们生活得更舒适，不必为一些事情忧心忡忡，有钱了，我们就不会挨饿，也能够拥有自己的房子。钱让我们感到安全！
“但无论花钱之前和之后，你还是你，内在并没有改变。这意味着金钱不会让你感到快乐幸福，只是让你感觉更舒适而已。”

[P13] “但舒适一般不会持续太久。比如一直吃最喜欢的食物，我们终将会厌倦它。幸福来自内心，是金钱买不到的！”
“很快你就会发现，许多让你幸福的事情并不昂贵，甚至是免费的！”
舒适
幸福

[P14] 那次谈话之后，当猫鼬想买一辆新自行车时，就会问自己到底能获得什么：是舒适还是真正的幸福？
他想了想，发现真正让自己开心幸福的是和朋友们一起骑车，而且这是免费的！金钱并不能买来好朋友。

[P15] 第二天，猫鼬想买一件新的燕尾服。他会得到幸福还是舒适呢？

啊！只是舒适而已。能给他带来快乐的其实是自信，而且他能够用很多种免费的方式获得自信。

[P16] 幸福有很多种，但最好的幸福总是免费的。

当然，金钱很重要。但金钱的主要作用是让我们感到舒适，
而不是提升幸福感。

幸福
满足感
愉悦感
舒适

[P17] 幸福指数：10/10 $ 
但并不能使我们的内心充满快乐！
幸福指数：10/10 $ 
总而言之，金钱只是一种工具。它让我们不为衣食住行发愁。
full_text_en:
[P1] $ If Animals Had Money
Money Is Not Everything
[US] Charlotte Dan, author [US] Adam Yong, illustrator, translated by Wang Siyao
CITIC Publishing Group

[P2] Money is the key to happiness! Whenever we buy what we want, we feel happy, right?

But most animals found that the meerkat, although he is the happiest among them, didn't spend much money! That's incredible.

[P3] For example, the meerkat's favorite toy isn't the superhero figures he received for Christmas, but the packaging boxes for those figures.
Superhero figures are cool, but those boxes can fulfill his imagination. From space to the deep sea, he imagines piloting this spaceship anywhere!
Happiness Index: 10/10 $

[P4] Last vacation, the meerkat and his two good brothers camped on the beach. It was so much fun!
All their food was picked or caught by themselves. The campsite didn't even have a toilet. But what the meerkat truly cared about was being with his friends.
Happiness Index: 10/10 $

[P5] The meerkat knows money is important, but he discovers that his happiness doesn't come from spending it.
His happiness comes from who he's with, from smiles and memories, and from his own feelings. Money can't buy these! So when he wants to feel even happier, he doesn't need to rely on money.

[P6] But the meerkat once didn't understand these principles. He used to think money was the source of happiness.
At that time, he believed the more money he spent, the happier he would be. Strangely, this approach actually made him very unhappy.

[P7] For example, a few years ago, the meerkat joined a luxury tour group. The cost of that trip was too high, and his friends couldn't afford it, so they couldn't join.
He spent money on all kinds of things, but it was still too boring. Throughout the trip, he kept calling his friends and missed home a lot.
Happiness Index:
2.5/10

[P8] Once, he spent a lot of money on a pair of beautiful red shoes. They were shiny and had air cushions! He couldn't wait to show them off to his friends.
But the shoes were really uncomfortable, and he never wore them again.
Happiness Index: 2/10

[P9] Once again, the meerkat went to the most upscale restaurant in town. To attend the dinner, he had to wear a tuxedo and use various forks during the meal.
But after eating, the meerkat was still hungry, so he had to go buy two hamburgers.

[P10] In the burger restaurant, the fox saw the meerkat wearing a tuxedo and asked him how his evening had been.

The meerkat couldn't help but complain, "Hey, I spent so much money trying to make myself happy, but it didn't work at all! I don't know what to do. Did I do something wrong?"

[P11] The fox immediately understood where the problem lay. He said, "I know now, I think you haven't understood where happiness comes from."

"You might not understand either, what money is actually for."

[P12] "Money can make our lives more comfortable, so we don't have to worry about certain things. With money, we won't go hungry, and we can have our own house. Money makes us feel safe!
"But whether before or after spending money, you are still you—your inner self hasn't changed. This means money won't make you feel happy or joyful; it only makes you feel more comfortable."

[P13] "But comfort usually doesn't last long. For example, if you keep eating your favorite food, you'll eventually get tired of it. Happiness comes from within, and money can't buy it!"
"Soon you'll discover that many things that make you happy aren't expensive, and some are even free!"
Comfort
Happiness

[P14] After that conversation, when the meerkat thought about buying a new bicycle, he would ask himself what he could really gain: comfort or true happiness?
He thought about it and realized that what truly made him happy was riding bikes with his friends, and it was free! Money couldn't buy good friends.

[P15] The next day, the meerkat wants to buy a new tuxedo. Will he get happiness or comfort?

Ah! Just comfort. What actually brings him joy is confidence, and he can gain confidence in many free ways.

[P16] There are many kinds of happiness, but the best happiness is always free.

Of course, money is important. But the main role of money is to make us feel comfortable,
not to increase our sense of happiness.

Happiness
Satisfaction
Pleasure
Comfort

[P17] Happiness Index: 10/10 $ 
But it cannot fill our hearts with joy!
Happiness Index: 10/10 $ 
In short, money is just a tool. It allows us not to worry about food, clothing, shelter, and transportation.
full_summary_zh:
[P1] 本页为绘本封面，标题为《金钱不是万能的》，副标题为《如果动物有钱了》，展示了一只穿着背带裤的猴子站在金钱堆前，背景有大量钞票图案，下方标注了作者、绘者、译者及出版社信息。
[P2] 本页通过对话形式探讨金钱与快乐的关系，左侧文字提出金钱能带来快乐的观点，右侧则指出猫鼬虽最快乐却并未花很多钱，引发思考。
[P3] 本页通过猫鼬的例子说明，真正的快乐并非来自昂贵的玩具，而是来自简单的包装盒，他用它想象自己驾驶飞船遨游宇宙，幸福指数达到满分。
[P4] 本页描绘了猫鼬和两个朋友在海滩露营的场景，他们自给自足，虽然条件简陋，但因能与朋友相伴而感到非常快乐，幸福指数达到满分。
[P5] 本页通过猫鼬的思考，总结出快乐并非来自金钱，而是源于与朋友相处、笑容、回忆和内心感受，强调金钱无法购买这些珍贵的情感体验。
[P6] 本页描绘了猫鼬过去认为花钱越多越快乐，但这种做法反而让他感到不快乐，通过画面中他往巨大心形容器里塞钱的场景，展现了他对金钱的错误认知。
[P7] 本页通过猫鼬参加豪华旅行团的经历，说明即使花费高昂，他依然感到无聊和想家，幸福指数仅为2.5/10，揭示金钱无法带来真正的快乐。
[P8] 猫鼬花了很多钱买了一双漂亮的红鞋，虽然很兴奋地向朋友炫耀，但鞋子不舒服，最终他不再穿，幸福指数仅为2/10。
[P9] 猫鼬为了赴宴去高档餐厅，穿着燕尾服使用各种叉子，但吃完后仍感到饥饿，只好再去买汉堡包。
[P10] 在汉堡店，狐狸遇到穿着燕尾服的猫鼬，猫鼬向他抱怨自己花了很多钱却无法获得快乐，感到困惑和沮丧。
[P11] 狐狸指出猫鼬没有理解快乐的来源，并质疑他是否明白金钱的真正用途，画面中两人站在装满钱的金罐旁，周围散落着钞票。
[P12] 本页通过猫鼬的内心独白，阐述了金钱的作用：它能带来舒适和安全感，但无法改变人的内在，也无法直接带来快乐和幸福。
[P13] 狐狸向猫鼬解释，舒适感会因重复而消退，真正的幸福源于内心，无法用金钱购买，并指出许多幸福的事情是免费的。画面中两人正看着一本打开的书，左侧页标题为“舒适”，右侧页标题为“幸福”，配以相应插图。
[P14] 猫鼬在考虑购买新自行车时，反思自己真正追求的是舒适还是幸福，并意识到与朋友一起骑车才是真正的快乐，且这种快乐是免费的，金钱无法买到友谊。
[P15] 猫鼬在浴室刷牙时思考购买新燕尾服是否能带来幸福，内心独白指出舒适只是短暂的，真正的快乐源于自信，而自信可以通过免费的方式获得。
[P16] 本页通过一个分层的心形图和文字说明，阐述了幸福、满足感、愉悦感和舒适之间的关系，强调金钱能带来舒适，但最好的幸福是免费的，源于内心。
[P17] 本页通过左右两幅对比画面，左侧展示富足但缺乏情感交流的家庭，右侧展示在雨中简单烧烤却充满欢笑的家庭，均标有‘幸福指数：10/10’，强调金钱虽能解决基本需求，但无法带来内心的快乐，真正的幸福源于情感与陪伴。
